answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate and 14-day contract expiration create a forced decision window. memory_c2 documents that switching to the low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—this is the only path that independently meets the finance mandate. However, assembly line running at 94% capacity with no buffer creates material delivery risk if onboarding friction occurs or if the vendor's quality/allocation proves inconsistent under margin pressure. Verifying memory_c2 confirms the prior onboarding speed and invoicing reliability. memory_c4 and memory_c6 show renegotiation and multi-year commitments can unlock margin recovery, but with 14 days remaining and no indication the incumbent will move sufficiently to meet an 18% target, these are unlikely to resolve the mandate. Adding a second source (memory_c3) would reduce single-point-of-failure risk but does not meet the cost mandate and consumes the one decision slot. Deferring (memory_c5) breaks the renewal timeline and removes the option to switch cleanly. Standard_experiment scale allows initial volume ramp with the low-cost vendor while preserving visibility into quality/delivery performance before full commitment. The decision is not fully reversible—switching back if performance fails would incur additional onboarding and cost volatility—hence downstream risk is flagged.
